source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 17: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
\(e^x\) ke saath ek mushkil sa fraction hai. Aise sawalon mein hamesha dekhiye ke kahin \(e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]\) ki shakal to nahi; agar ho to jawab seedha \(e^xf(x)\).
Square kholte hain: \((1 - x)^2 = 1 - 2x + x^2 = (1 + x^2) - 2x\).
Is se integrand do hisson mein toot jata hai: \(\frac{1}{1+x^2}\) aur \(\frac{-2x}{(1+x^2)^2}\), aur doosra pehle ka derivative hai!
Plan: square kholein, \(f\) aur \(f'\) pehchanein, Note lagayein (ya parts se dikhayein ke integrals cancel hote hain).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int e^x\left(\frac{1 - x}{1 + x^2}\right)^2 dx\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: integrand ko \(e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]\) banayenge, \(f(x) = \frac{1}{1+x^2}\); phir Note (\(g(x) = x\)): \(\int e^x[f + f']\,dx = e^xf + c\).

Square kholein
\[\dfrac{(1 - x)^2}{(1 + x^2)^2} = \dfrac{(1 + x^2) - 2x}{(1 + x^2)^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} - \dfrac{2x}{(1 + x^2)^2}\]
Kyun: \((1 - x)^2 = 1 - 2x + x^2\), aur \(1 + x^2\) ko ikattha likha taa ke ek term cancel ho sake.

\(f\) aur \(f'\) pehchanein
\[f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} \Rightarrow f'(x) = \dfrac{-2x}{(1 + x^2)^2}\]
\[\int e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]\,dx\]
Kyun: \((1 + x^2)^{-1}\) ka derivative chain rule se \(-1\cdot(1 + x^2)^{-2}\cdot 2x\). Yani doosra hissa bilkul pehle ka derivative hai.

Jawab \(e^xf\) kyun (parts se)
\[\int e^xf\,dx = f e^x - \int e^x f'\,dx\]
\[\int e^x(f + f')\,dx = e^xf + c\]
Kyun: \(\int e^xf\,dx\) par parts (\(f\) first, \(e^x\) second) se \(-\int e^xf'\,dx\) nikalta hai, jo doosre hisse ko cancel kar deta hai. Yahi kitab ka Note hai.

Jawab
\[= \dfrac{e^x}{1 + x^2} + c\]
Kyun: \(e^xf(x)\) mein \(f = \frac{1}{1+x^2}\) rakh diya.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{e^x}{1 + x^2}\right) = e^x\left[\dfrac{1}{1+x^2} - \dfrac{2x}{(1+x^2)^2}\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{e^x(1 - x)^2}{(1 + x^2)^2}\]
Kyun: product rule lagaya, phir step 1 ulta: bracket \(\frac{(1 - x)^2}{(1+x^2)^2}\) hai. Integrand mil gaya.
